text:
Dallas arrives off a 3-1 win over Columbus three days ago, 3-2-0 in its last five and missing Kyle Capobianco and Oskar Bäck. Washington is coming off a 5-1 loss to Minnesota two days ago, which ended its three-game winning streak. The Capitals are also 3-2-0 over five and are without Vincent Desharnais. This is the first meeting of the season; the Stars won both games last year.

The teams look close on the ice. At five on five, Dallas has taken 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games and Washington 53%. Our model projects 3.05 goals for the Stars and 2.96 for the Capitals. The gap is on special teams. Washington has taken 4.5 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays, and its penalty kill allows 0.82 expected goals a game against Dallas's 0.55.

In net, projected starter Jake Oettinger is 9.7 goals saved above expected (how many goals he has stopped beyond what the shots should have produced) this season, against 3.9 for projected Washington starter Logan Thompson. Last season Thompson was at +28.2 over 58 games, Oettinger at +2.2 over 54.

Alex Tuch has 10 goals in 12 games, as RMNB posted, and we give him a 35% chance of scoring. Wyatt Johnston is Dallas's best bet at 39%. Mikko Rantanen is one point from 800 for his career. Tom Wilson has one point in his last ten games on chances that point to more.
